purpose: machine-facing knowledge base of concrete entrepreneurial decision work-units spanning startup validation, go-to-market, funding, and growth, for planning, evaluation, prioritization, risk control, and session-bounded execution within the knowledge-searcher meta-KB
assumptions: subdomain of business strategy and operations modeled as session-bounded stepwise execution for heavy LLM-assisted venture-building work
no observed dataset supplied; all metrics are heuristic priors
nodes are concrete entrepreneurial decision work-units, not abstract themes
single-venture early-to-growth-stage lens; corporate intrapreneurship and M&A are out of scope
key references are Ries The Lean Startup and Osterwalder and Pigneur Business Model Generation
exclusions: hiring and HR process detail beyond scaling decisions
exit, M&A, and IPO execution mechanics

competency_questions.question: Which concrete customer problem is validated as worth solving and for which beachhead segment?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answer cites PROBLEM_DISCOVERY and CUSTOMER_DISCOVERY outputs

competency_questions.question: What evidence threshold confirms a problem and its early-adopter segment before building?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answer cites PROBLEM_DISCOVERY and CUSTOMER_DISCOVERY acceptance_tests

competency_questions.question: What is the differentiated value proposition and how does the business model capture it?
What is the smallest MVP that tests the riskiest assumption and how is learning measured?
What measurable signals indicate product-market fit across cohorts?
When should the venture persevere, pivot, or kill, and on what evidence?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answer cites PIVOT_DECISION criteria and dependencies

competency_questions.question: How are positioning and value-based pricing set to capture value competitively?
Which channels and conversion funnel match the buyer, price, and economics?
Do the unit economics show that growth creates rather than destroys value?
Should the venture bootstrap or raise, and how is runway managed to the next milestone?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answer cites BOOTSTRAPPING, FUNDRAISING, and RUNWAY_BURN_MANAGEMENT

competency_questions.question: How does each financing round affect dilution and the cap table irreversibly?
Which leading traction metrics and growth engine compound demand within economic limits?
When is the venture ready to launch go-to-market and scale operations safely?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answer cites GO_TO_MARKET and SCALING_OPERATIONS fit gates

competency_questions.question: What operating cadence keeps strategy executing as the team grows?

glossary.definition: smallest build that tests the riskiest assumption with real users
evidence that a product satisfies a strong market need with durable retention and pull
structured change of strategy that preserves validated learning
the specific value delivered to a segment and why it beats alternatives
nine-block description of how value is created, delivered, and captured
per-customer revenue and cost dynamics including CAC, LTV, and payback
cost to acquire one paying customer
expected gross margin from a customer over its lifetime
reduction in ownership percentage from issuing new equity
record of equity ownership, options, and preferences
months of operation remaining at current burn
funding growth from revenue and minimal outside capital
single metric that best captures delivered customer value
repeatable loop (sticky, viral, or paid) that compounds growth
initial narrow segment targeted before broadening

evidence_label_policy.rationale: no observed dataset supplied; all values heuristic

source_registry.description: heuristic priors from established entrepreneurship and business-model literature and practice; supports estimated scores, weights, and relations
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Ries The Lean Startup; Osterwalder and Pigneur Business Model Generation

nodes.definition: Identify and validate a concrete, painful, frequent customer problem worth solving before committing to a solution.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: ten or more interviews contradict the assumed top pain point

pros.claim: anchors the venture on a real pain, reducing build-wrong-thing risk
pros.example: Ries-style get-out-of-the-building interviews surface that users hate manual reconciliation

pros.claim: cheap to run relative to building
pros.example: 20 problem interviews cost days, not a build cycle

cons.claim: interview bias and leading questions produce false positives
cons.example: asking 'would you use X' yields polite yeses

cons.claim: problem may be real but not monetizable
cons.example: painful but nobody pays to solve it

nodes.definition: Define and locate the specific early-adopter segment and decision-makers who feel the problem most acutely.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: beachhead segment shows no willingness to engage after sustained outreach

pros.claim: targets scarce validation effort on reachable buyers
pros.example: focus on 3 design-partner accounts not the whole TAM

pros.claim: early adopters tolerate rough MVPs
pros.example: they trade polish for early access

cons.claim: early adopters may not generalize to mainstream
cons.example: visionaries buy differently than pragmatists

cons.claim: segment too narrow starves growth
cons.example: niche has no expansion path

nodes.definition: Articulate the specific value the product delivers to a segment and why it beats alternatives, mapping pains to gains.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: buyers cannot restate the value proposition unprompted in interviews

pros.claim: forces fit between customer jobs and offering
pros.example: Osterwalder value-proposition canvas aligns relievers to pains

pros.claim: becomes the spine of messaging and pricing
pros.example: one crisp promise drives the whole funnel

cons.claim: easy to overclaim differentiation
cons.example: '10x better' with no proof erodes trust

cons.claim: value clear to founder but not to buyer
cons.example: insider framing confuses outsiders

nodes.definition: Specify how the venture creates, delivers, and captures value across the nine business-model-canvas building blocks.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a core canvas block (revenue or channel) is invalidated by market evidence

pros.claim: makes value capture and delivery explicit and testable
pros.example: Business Model Generation canvas exposes a missing revenue stream

pros.claim: reveals interdependencies between blocks
pros.example: channel choice constrains cost structure

cons.claim: canvas can stay a static poster, not a tested hypothesis set
cons.example: filled once, never validated

cons.claim: model coherence ignored across blocks
cons.example: free acquisition with high-touch delivery does not pencil

nodes.definition: Scope the smallest build that validates the riskiest assumption with real users while minimizing wasted effort.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the MVP ships but produces no interpretable learning signal

pros.claim: converts assumptions into measurable learning fast
pros.example: Lean Startup concierge MVP tests demand before any code

pros.claim: caps sunk cost before product-market fit
pros.example: kill criteria limit downside

cons.claim: scope creep turns MVP into a full product
cons.example: 'just one more feature' delays learning

cons.claim: too minimal to produce a valid signal
cons.example: broken MVP measures frustration not demand

nodes.definition: Design falsifiable validation experiments with explicit hypotheses, metrics, and success thresholds.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a previously significant validation result fails to replicate

pros.claim: replaces opinion with falsifiable evidence
pros.example: define fit as 40 percent would-be-very-disappointed before launch

pros.claim: separates actionable from vanity metrics
pros.example: cohort retention over raw signups

cons.claim: underpowered tests mislead
cons.example: tiny samples produce noise read as signal

cons.claim: metric gaming distorts learning
cons.example: optimizing a proxy that does not predict revenue

nodes.definition: Determine whether the product satisfies a strong market need with evidence of retention, demand pull, and organic growth.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: retention or referral signals fall back below the fit threshold for two cohorts

pros.claim: is the precondition for scaling spend safely
pros.example: flattening retention curve signals durable demand

pros.claim: creates demand pull that lowers acquisition cost
pros.example: users refer others without incentives

cons.claim: fit is fragile and segment-specific
cons.example: fit in one niche evaporates in the next

cons.claim: false-positive fit from a hot launch
cons.example: launch spike mistaken for durable retention

nodes.definition: Decide whether to persevere, pivot, or kill based on validated-learning evidence against pre-set criteria.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: validated learning materially contradicts the core thesis

pros.claim: prevents zombie persistence on a failing model
pros.example: runway-aware pivot redeploys capital before insolvency

pros.claim: structured pivot preserves validated learning
pros.example: keep the customer, change the solution

cons.claim: pivoting too often destroys accumulated learning
cons.example: serial pivots never reach depth

cons.claim: sunk-cost bias delays necessary pivots
cons.example: emotional attachment overrides evidence

nodes.definition: Establish how the product is perceived relative to alternatives in the mind of the target buyer.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: target buyers consistently place the product in a different category than intended

pros.claim: frames the competitive set in the venture favor
pros.example: choosing the category sets the comparison and the budget line

pros.claim: aligns sales, marketing, and product on one story
pros.example: one frame reduces message drift

cons.claim: wrong category invites unwinnable comparisons
cons.example: positioning against incumbents on their terms loses

cons.claim: repositioning is costly once established
cons.example: brand inertia resists reframing

nodes.definition: Choose a pricing model, metric, and level that captures value, supports unit economics, and fits the buyer.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: willingness-to-pay evidence diverges materially from the set price

pros.claim: is the highest-leverage profit driver
pros.example: a value-based price metric lifts margin without new product

pros.claim: pricing metric shapes customer behavior and alignment
pros.example: per-seat versus per-usage changes incentives

cons.claim: mispricing silently caps growth or margin
cons.example: underpricing leaves money and signals low value

cons.claim: price changes risk churn and trust
cons.example: raising prices on existing users triggers backlash

nodes.definition: Select and sequence acquisition and distribution channels that match the buyer, price point, and economics.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the lead channel CAC rises above payback tolerance

pros.claim: channel-price fit determines viable acquisition cost
pros.example: low-touch self-serve fits low ACV; field sales fits high ACV

pros.claim: channel choice constrains the whole GTM motion
pros.example: PLG and enterprise sales need different orgs

cons.claim: channel-price mismatch makes CAC unviable
cons.example: field sales on a 20-dollar-per-month product loses money

cons.claim: channel saturation erodes returns over time
cons.example: early channel decays as competitors crowd in

nodes.definition: Design and instrument the conversion funnel from awareness to closed revenue with stage metrics and bottleneck control.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a downstream funnel stage becomes the new binding constraint

pros.claim: locates the binding conversion constraint
pros.example: stage instrumentation reveals the trial-to-paid drop

pros.claim: makes revenue forecastable from funnel math
pros.example: conversion rates make pipeline predictable

cons.claim: optimizing one stage can starve another
cons.example: top-of-funnel growth without close capacity stalls

cons.claim: funnel metrics decay as channels shift
cons.example: yesterday conversion math misleads tomorrow

nodes.definition: Model per-customer economics (CAC, LTV, payback, contribution margin) to test whether growth creates value.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: cohort-level LTV over CAC falls below the viability threshold

pros.claim: separates profitable growth from value-destroying growth
pros.example: LTV over CAC below 3 with long payback signals unscalable economics

pros.claim: gates the decision to pour capital into scaling
pros.example: positive contribution margin precedes spend

cons.claim: early LTV estimates are unreliable
cons.example: short history overstates lifetime value

cons.claim: blended metrics hide bad cohorts
cons.example: aggregate hides unprofitable channels

nodes.definition: Fund growth from revenue and minimal capital to retain control and impose capital discipline.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a funded competitor growth rate threatens to foreclose the market

pros.claim: retains ownership and forces capital discipline
pros.example: default-alive bootstrapping avoids dilution

pros.claim: revenue-funded growth proves model viability
pros.example: customers, not investors, fund the next step

cons.claim: caps growth speed in winner-take-most markets
cons.example: slow growth cedes the market to funded rivals

cons.claim: undercapitalization risks stalling at a local maximum
cons.example: no buffer for a bad quarter

nodes.definition: Decide whether, when, and how much external equity to raise, and run the round to credible investors.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the fundraising environment or milestone plan shifts enough to change the raise decision

pros.claim: buys speed and runway to capture a time-sensitive market
pros.example: a round funds the leap a competitor cannot match

pros.claim: credible investors add governance and network
pros.example: the right VC opens doors beyond capital

cons.claim: raising too early or too much over-dilutes and sets a hard valuation
cons.example: a high priced round becomes a down-round trap

cons.claim: misaligned investors distort strategy
cons.example: growth pressure forces premature scaling

nodes.definition: Manage ownership structure, option pool, dilution, and founder and investor splits across financing events.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a financing or grant decision would materially and irreversibly alter ownership

pros.claim: keeps founder incentives and control aligned across rounds
pros.example: modeling pro-forma dilution prevents nasty surprises

pros.claim: clean cap table eases future rounds and exit
pros.example: investors diligence a tidy table fast

cons.claim: cap-table mistakes are hard or impossible to reverse
cons.example: an oversized early grant cannot be clawed back

cons.claim: liquidation preferences can wipe out common at exit
cons.example: stacked prefs leave founders with little

nodes.definition: Manage cash runway, burn rate, and spending milestones to stay solvent and reach the next value inflection.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: runway falls below the threshold needed to reach the next milestone

pros.claim: keeps the venture solvent to its next milestone
pros.example: an 18-month runway buys time to reach fit

pros.claim: burn discipline preserves optionality
pros.example: slower burn keeps pivot and raise options open

cons.claim: running out of cash is terminal and irreversible
cons.example: insolvency ends the venture regardless of promise

cons.claim: over-conservatism starves necessary investment
cons.example: cutting growth spend can stall the company

nodes.definition: Define and track the leading growth metrics that evidence durable demand and inform investment decisions.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the north-star metric decouples from revenue or value

pros.claim: a single north-star metric aligns the team on real value
pros.example: DAU-to-value metric beats vanity downloads

pros.claim: cohort tracking exposes decay early
pros.example: cohort curves reveal churn before revenue shows it

cons.claim: wrong north-star metric optimizes the wrong thing
cons.example: chasing signups over retention misallocates effort

cons.claim: metric proliferation dilutes focus
cons.example: fifty dashboards, no decision

nodes.definition: Identify and engineer the repeatable, scalable growth engine (viral, paid, or sticky) that compounds traction.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the chosen growth engine efficiency decays below viability

pros.claim: a working engine makes growth predictable and compounding
pros.example: Lean Startup sticky, viral, and paid engines define the loop

pros.claim: matching engine to economics prevents waste
pros.example: paid engine only works with payback under target

cons.claim: running multiple half-built engines wastes effort
cons.example: viral and paid pursued at once dilute both

cons.claim: engine that ignores retention leaks growth
cons.example: filling a leaky bucket burns cash

nodes.definition: Integrate positioning, pricing, channels, and funnel into a coherent launch-and-acquire plan for the beachhead.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: fit or channel evidence invalidates a core GTM assumption

pros.claim: aligns all GTM levers on one beachhead motion
pros.example: positioning, price, channel, and funnel reinforce one motion

pros.claim: sequenced beachhead-first avoids spreading thin
pros.example: win one segment before broadening

cons.claim: GTM launched before fit wastes acquisition spend
cons.example: scaling acquisition pre-fit burns the runway

cons.claim: incoherent levers cancel each other
cons.example: premium positioning with discount pricing confuses buyers

nodes.definition: Scale team, processes, and systems to grow throughput without breaking quality, culture, or unit economics.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: unit economics or quality metrics degrade as scale increases

pros.claim: systematizes what works so growth does not break it
pros.example: documented playbooks let new hires reproduce results

pros.claim: right-sized hiring protects unit economics
pros.example: scaling headcount with revenue, not ahead of it

cons.claim: premature scaling is the top startup killer
cons.example: building org and process before fit wastes capital

cons.claim: scaling can dilute culture and quality
cons.example: fast hiring erodes standards and cohesion

nodes.definition: Establish the recurring planning, review, and decision rhythm (goals, metrics reviews, retrospectives) that runs the venture.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the operating cadence stops producing decisions or no longer fits team size

pros.claim: a steady cadence converts strategy into executed iteration
pros.example: weekly metric reviews catch drift early

pros.claim: shared rhythm aligns a growing team
pros.example: OKRs cascade focus across functions

cons.claim: cadence can become ritual without decisions
cons.example: meetings that review but never decide

cons.claim: over-heavy process slows a small team
cons.example: too much ceremony for a five-person startup

edges.why_related: a validated problem scopes which customers to target
edges.benefit_of_coupling: focuses discovery on those who feel the pain
edges.risk_of_conflict: skipping it targets the wrong segment
edges.resolution_rule: problem evidence dominates; redo discovery if problem shifts

edges.why_related: value must answer a validated problem
edges.benefit_of_coupling: grounds value claims in real pain
edges.risk_of_conflict: value built on assumed pain misfires

edges.why_related: the canvas captures value around the value proposition
edges.benefit_of_coupling: keeps the model centered on value
edges.risk_of_conflict: model without a value core is unfounded
edges.resolution_rule: value proposition dominates the canvas center

edges.why_related: the MVP tests the value proposition riskiest claim
edges.benefit_of_coupling: aims the build at the key risk
edges.risk_of_conflict: MVP without a value target wastes effort
edges.resolution_rule: value risk ranking dominates MVP scope

edges.why_related: the riskiest canvas assumption sets the MVP target
edges.risk_of_conflict: testing the wrong assumption wastes a cycle
edges.example: riskiest block becomes the MVP test

edges.why_related: experiments are designed around the MVP learning goal
edges.risk_of_conflict: an MVP without a test yields no learning

edges.why_related: fit is judged from experiment evidence
edges.risk_of_conflict: fit declared without evidence is a guess

edges.why_related: fit requires a real product in users hands
edges.risk_of_conflict: fit cannot be judged without an MVP

edges.why_related: pivot decisions read from validated learning
edges.risk_of_conflict: pivoting on opinion thrashes

edges.why_related: the fit verdict drives persevere, pivot, or kill
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring fit prolongs a dead model
edges.resolution_rule: fit evidence dominates persevere or kill

edges.why_related: positioning expresses the value proposition competitively
edges.risk_of_conflict: positioning detached from value confuses buyers

edges.why_related: positioning is most credible once fit is evidenced
edges.benefit_of_coupling: avoids positioning a product nobody wants
edges.risk_of_conflict: positioning pre-fit risks rework

edges.why_related: the revenue-stream design constrains pricing
edges.risk_of_conflict: pricing outside the model breaks it

edges.why_related: value-based pricing anchors price to delivered value
edges.risk_of_conflict: cost-plus pricing leaves value uncaptured

edges.why_related: unit economics bound the feasible price band
edges.risk_of_conflict: a price that breaks economics is unsustainable
edges.resolution_rule: economics constrain price; price must satisfy economics

edges.why_related: the buyer profile determines viable channels
edges.risk_of_conflict: channel-buyer mismatch wastes spend

edges.why_related: price point bounds the affordable acquisition channel
edges.benefit_of_coupling: keeps CAC viable for the price
edges.risk_of_conflict: high-touch channels break low price points
edges.resolution_rule: price constrains channel; channel must fit CAC

edges.why_related: channels feed the top of the funnel
edges.risk_of_conflict: an unmapped channel cannot be optimized

edges.why_related: price directly changes LTV and contribution margin
edges.risk_of_conflict: mispricing corrupts the economics model
edges.example: a price rise lifts LTV over CAC
edges.resolution_rule: price feeds economics; recompute on any price change

edges.why_related: funnel conversion rates determine effective CAC
edges.risk_of_conflict: stale conversion misstates CAC
edges.resolution_rule: funnel data feeds CAC; recompute on conversion change

edges.why_related: positive unit economics enable revenue-funded growth
edges.risk_of_conflict: bootstrapping on bad economics stalls
edges.resolution_rule: economics evidence dominates the bootstrap decision

edges.why_related: economics justify the raise size and use of funds
edges.benefit_of_coupling: grounds the raise in a model
edges.risk_of_conflict: raising without economics misallocates capital
edges.example: LTV over CAC supports the ask

edges.why_related: investors fund a coherent, scalable model
edges.risk_of_conflict: an incoherent model fails diligence

edges.why_related: bootstrapping and raising trade control and ownership against growth speed
edges.risk_of_conflict: pursuing both half-heartedly stalls growth and dilutes focus
edges.example: slow bootstrapped growth versus a funded sprint
edges.resolution_rule: choose by market clock and economics; if winner-take-most and economics proven, favor raising, else bootstrap

edges.why_related: each round reshapes the cap table and dilution
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged dilution surprises founders
edges.example: a round triggers a cap-table update

edges.why_related: raised capital extends runway and resets burn planning
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring it misjudges solvency
edges.example: a round resets the runway clock
edges.resolution_rule: new capital feeds runway; replan burn on close

edges.why_related: burn planning depends on per-unit cash dynamics
edges.risk_of_conflict: burn divorced from economics misleads

edges.why_related: shrinking runway can trigger a pivot-or-kill revisit
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring runway delays inevitable decisions
edges.example: short runway forces a faster verdict
edges.resolution_rule: when runway crosses the decision horizon, escalate the pivot decision; stop once a decision is recorded

edges.why_related: traction metrics extend fit signals into growth tracking
edges.risk_of_conflict: tracking growth pre-fit measures noise
edges.example: fit cohorts seed the north star

edges.why_related: GTM executes the chosen positioning
edges.risk_of_conflict: GTM without positioning drifts

edges.why_related: GTM operationalizes the channel plan
edges.risk_of_conflict: GTM without channels is abstract
edges.resolution_rule: channel plan dominates the GTM motion

edges.why_related: the instrumented funnel runs the GTM acquisition
edges.risk_of_conflict: GTM without a funnel cannot optimize

edges.why_related: scaling GTM acquisition is gated on fit evidence
edges.risk_of_conflict: launching GTM pre-fit wastes the runway
edges.resolution_rule: fit evidence gates GTM scale; do not scale acquisition before fit

edges.why_related: the growth engine is engineered from traction signals
edges.benefit_of_coupling: targets the engine at real loops
edges.risk_of_conflict: an engine without metrics is blind

edges.why_related: economics bound which growth engine is viable
edges.risk_of_conflict: an uneconomic engine burns cash
edges.resolution_rule: economics constrain engine choice; engine must respect payback

edges.why_related: scaling operations is gated on durable fit
edges.risk_of_conflict: scaling pre-fit is the top startup killer
edges.resolution_rule: fit evidence gates scaling; never scale ops before fit

edges.why_related: scaling must preserve unit economics
edges.risk_of_conflict: scaling that breaks economics destroys value
edges.resolution_rule: economics constrain scaling; halt scale if economics degrade

edges.why_related: a repeatable GTM motion is the basis for scaling
edges.risk_of_conflict: scaling an unproven motion multiplies waste
edges.resolution_rule: proven GTM dominates the scale decision

edges.why_related: the metric set drives the recurring review rhythm
edges.risk_of_conflict: cadence without metrics is ritual

edges.why_related: a working growth engine should precede heavy operational scaling
edges.risk_of_conflict: scaling without an engine wastes capacity

conflict_axes.trigger: pressure to scale or launch before fit is evidenced
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: validation evidence dominates; do not scale acquisition or operations before fit signals pass the defined bar
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: team proposes scaling spend while retention is below the fit threshold
conflict_axes.example: founder wants to launch ads before retention flattens

conflict_axes.trigger: deciding whether to raise equity or grow on revenue
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if market is winner-take-most and economics are proven, capital access dominates; otherwise retain control via bootstrapping
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a funded competitor threatens to foreclose the market
conflict_axes.example: raise a large round versus stay default-alive

conflict_axes.trigger: lowering price to grow volume erodes margin and payback
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: unit economics dominate; price may drop only while payback stays within tolerance
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: discounting raises signups but pushes payback past tolerance
conflict_axes.example: cut price to win volume versus hold price for margin

conflict_axes.trigger: broadening the target market before winning the beachhead
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: beachhead focus dominates until fit is proven in the segment, then breadth is allowed
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: expanding to new segments while the first is unconverted
conflict_axes.example: serve everyone now versus dominate one niche first

conflict_axes.trigger: validated learning contradicts the current thesis but the team is attached
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: validated learning dominates sunk cost; pivot when evidence contradicts the thesis and runway allows
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: metrics keep missing yet the team keeps iterating the same model
conflict_axes.example: keep pushing the current model versus change direction

conflict_axes.trigger: spending on growth shortens runway below the safe milestone buffer
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: solvency dominates; growth spend is capped so runway covers the next milestone plus buffer
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: growth budget would cut runway under the next-milestone threshold
conflict_axes.example: pour cash into growth versus extend runway

conflict_axes.trigger: reporting flattering metrics that do not predict value or revenue
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: actionable metrics dominate; the north star must predict value and tie to economics
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: dashboards highlight signups while retention and revenue stall
conflict_axes.example: celebrate downloads versus track retained revenue

conflict_axes.trigger: adding process and cadence overhead too early slows experimentation
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: speed dominates pre-fit; process is introduced only as team size and scale require it
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: heavy planning ceremony imposed on a tiny pre-fit team
conflict_axes.example: add OKRs and rituals now versus stay lean until scaling

edge_cases.trigger: a launch spike is mistaken for durable product-market fit
edge_cases.failure_mode: premature scaling on a false-positive fit signal
edge_cases.example: a Product Hunt spike fades to near-zero retention within weeks
edge_cases.detection_method: compare retention across at least two cohorts before declaring fit
resolution: require fit to hold across two cohorts

edge_cases.trigger: the north-star metric is a vanity metric decoupled from revenue
edge_cases.failure_mode: team optimizes a metric that does not predict value
edge_cases.example: signups rise while paid retention falls
edge_cases.detection_method: test correlation between north-star metric and retained revenue
resolution: replace metric with one that predicts value

edge_cases.trigger: MVP scope expands beyond the riskiest assumption
edge_cases.failure_mode: build cost balloons and learning is delayed
edge_cases.example: the MVP grows three extra modules before any user test
edge_cases.detection_method: check each MVP feature maps to the one riskiest assumption
resolution: cut features not tied to the test

edge_cases.trigger: LTV is overstated from short history or blended cohorts
edge_cases.failure_mode: scaling is justified on unprofitable economics
edge_cases.example: blended LTV/CAC of 4 hides a channel running at 1.2
edge_cases.detection_method: recompute LTV by cohort with conservative retention assumptions

edge_cases.trigger: a high-touch channel is used for a low price point
edge_cases.failure_mode: CAC exceeds viable payback and burn accelerates
edge_cases.example: field sales deployed for a $15/month product
edge_cases.detection_method: compare channel CAC against price-implied payback tolerance

edge_cases.trigger: a round closes without modeling pro-forma dilution
edge_cases.failure_mode: founders are unexpectedly and irreversibly over-diluted
edge_cases.example: an option-pool refresh plus a large round halves founder stake unexpectedly
edge_cases.detection_method: require a pro-forma cap table and dilution model before signing terms
resolution: model dilution per scenario before signing

edge_cases.trigger: runway is misjudged and cash crosses the danger line late
edge_cases.failure_mode: the venture becomes insolvent before a pivot or raise can close
edge_cases.example: a fundraise slips two months and the company runs out of cash
edge_cases.detection_method: track runway monthly against milestones with a downside scenario

edge_cases.trigger: the venture pivots repeatedly without preserving learning
edge_cases.failure_mode: accumulated validated learning is lost and depth is never reached
edge_cases.example: four pivots in six months reset the company each time
edge_cases.detection_method: check each pivot preserves prior validated learning and names a pivot type
resolution: require a decision record per pivot

edge_cases.trigger: the bootstrap-versus-raise tradeoff is modeled as a dependency
edge_cases.failure_mode: a genuine conflict is hidden, distorting priority and workflow
edge_cases.example: the model treats raising as a prerequisite for bootstrapping
edge_cases.detection_method: verify the bootstrap-raise relation is encoded as a conflict edge with signed_tension below zero

edge_cases.trigger: go-to-market acquisition is scaled before fit evidence
edge_cases.failure_mode: acquisition spend burns runway on a product without pull
edge_cases.example: paid acquisition scaled while retention is still decaying
edge_cases.detection_method: confirm the GTM scale gate requires passing fit signals
resolution: block acquisition scale until fit gate passes

edge_cases.trigger: price is set by cost-plus instead of delivered value
edge_cases.failure_mode: the venture underprices and caps growth and margin
edge_cases.example: a tool saving customers $10k is priced at $200 on cost-plus logic
edge_cases.detection_method: check price is anchored to quantified buyer value not internal cost

edge_cases.trigger: scaling decisions are hard-locked before fit and economics gates pass
edge_cases.failure_mode: the venture commits irreversibly on unproven foundations
edge_cases.example: a scaling hiring plan is locked while economics are still negative
edge_cases.detection_method: verify no scaling artifact is hard-locked before its dependency and review gates pass

workflow.objective: validate a real problem and locate the beachhead segment
entry_criteria: venture idea and target hypotheses exist
exit_criteria: problem and segment validated with evidence
workflow.do_first_because: problem and customer evidence is the irreversible foundation; building on a wrong problem causes maximal rework

workflow.objective: define the differentiated value and the business model around it
exit_criteria: value and model hypotheses documented and ranked
workflow.do_first_because: value and model frame every later test; defining them early prevents building the wrong thing

workflow.objective: scope the MVP for the riskiest assumption and design falsifiable experiments
exit_criteria: MVP scoped and experiments designed with pre-set thresholds
workflow.do_first_because: scoping the MVP and tests before building caps sunk cost and yields interpretable learning

workflow.objective: assess product-market fit and decide persevere, pivot, or kill
exit_criteria: fit verdict reached and persevere/pivot/kill recorded
workflow.do_first_because: fit is the gate for all downstream scaling; a wrong call here wastes the most capital

workflow.objective: set competitive positioning and value-based pricing
exit_criteria: positioning and pricing validated against buyers and economics
workflow.do_first_because: positioning and price frame the channel and funnel; setting them first avoids GTM rework

workflow.objective: select acquisition channels and instrument the conversion funnel
exit_criteria: channels chosen and funnel instrumented with baselines
workflow.do_first_because: channel-price fit and funnel instrumentation are needed before computing trustworthy economics

workflow.objective: validate unit economics and choose the capital strategy with runway and cap-table control
exit_criteria: economics validated and capital strategy decided with runway and cap-table modeled
workflow.do_first_because: capital and scaling decisions are gated on validated economics; getting economics first prevents value-destroying growth

workflow.objective: define traction metrics and engineer the repeatable growth engine
exit_criteria: traction metrics defined and one growth engine validated
workflow.do_first_because: a working, economical engine must exist before scaling acquisition and operations

workflow.objective: integrate positioning, pricing, channels, and funnel into a coherent launch motion
entry_criteria: positioning, channels, funnel, and fit available
exit_criteria: coherent GTM motion defined and gated on fit
workflow.do_first_because: a coherent, fit-gated GTM motion is the prerequisite for safe scaling

workflow.objective: scale operations on proven foundations and run an operating cadence
entry_criteria: fit, economics, and a repeatable GTM motion exist
exit_criteria: operations scaled within economics and a decision cadence running
workflow.do_first_because: scaling is last because it multiplies whatever exists; doing it before fit and economics is the top startup killer

dominance_rules.trigger: scaling or launch is proposed before fit and economics are evidenced
dominance_rules.rule: risk control dominates speed; do not scale before fit and economics gates pass
dominance_rules.example: block ad spend scale-up until retention flattens

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node depends on an unfinished prerequisite
dominance_rules.rule: dependency precedence dominates raw value ordering
dominance_rules.example: do not finalize pricing before unit economics inputs exist

dominance_rules.trigger: a metric is stated with false numeric precision beyond its evidence
dominance_rules.required_action: downgrade to heuristic and widen uncertainty
dominance_rules.example: an LTV given to four decimals on two months of data is labeled heuristic

dominance_rules.trigger: an artifact is proposed for lock before its acceptance tests pass
dominance_rules.rule: QA dominates locking; tests must pass before any lock
dominance_rules.example: a scaling plan cannot be locked while economics are negative

dominance_rules.trigger: an irreversible capital, dilution, or scaling decision is reached
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation for irreversible decisions
dominance_rules.required_action: require human approval and a decision record
dominance_rules.example: a financing term sheet requires human sign-off

dominance_rules.trigger: growth spend would push runway below the next-milestone buffer
dominance_rules.required_action: cap growth spend to preserve milestone runway
dominance_rules.example: freeze a growth budget that would cut runway under six months

dominance_rules.trigger: price cuts or channel spend would break payback tolerance
dominance_rules.required_action: keep price and spend within payback tolerance
dominance_rules.example: reject a discount that pushes payback beyond the target

dominance_rules.trigger: validated learning contradicts the current thesis
dominance_rules.required_action: pivot or kill per pre-set criteria
dominance_rules.example: pivot when two cohorts fail the fit bar despite team attachment

dominance_rules.trigger: market broadening is proposed before the beachhead is won
dominance_rules.rule: beachhead focus dominates breadth until fit is proven
dominance_rules.example: defer multi-segment expansion until the first segment converts

dominance_rules.trigger: adding nodes or edges would break schema or reference integrity
dominance_rules.example: do not add an edge whose endpoint node does not exist

anti_rework_rules.rule: validate the problem before building any solution
anti_rework_rules.rationale: building on an unvalidated problem causes maximal rework
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: an MVP exists with no validated problem statement
anti_rework_rules.example: a team codes for months before any problem interview

anti_rework_rules.rule: define the value proposition before finalizing the business model
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a model without a value core must be redone
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: canvas blocks filled with no value map
anti_rework_rules.example: revenue streams set before knowing what value is sold

anti_rework_rules.rule: rank the riskiest assumption before scoping the MVP
anti_rework_rules.rationale: testing the wrong assumption wastes a build cycle
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: MVP scope not tied to a ranked assumption
anti_rework_rules.example: an MVP tests a low-risk feature instead of the key risk

anti_rework_rules.rule: set hypotheses and success thresholds before running experiments
anti_rework_rules.rationale: thresholds set after seeing data invite bias
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a fit threshold defined after results arrive
anti_rework_rules.example: declaring fit by moving the bar to match the data

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not scale acquisition or operations before fit evidence
anti_rework_rules.rationale: scaling pre-fit burns runway on a product without pull
anti_rework_rules.example: paid spend ramped before the retention curve flattens

anti_rework_rules.rule: validate unit economics before raising or heavy growth spend
anti_rework_rules.rationale: capital poured into bad economics destroys value
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a raise pitched with no cohort economics
anti_rework_rules.example: scaling a paid engine with LTV/CAC below 1

anti_rework_rules.rule: model pro-forma dilution before signing any financing terms
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a term sheet signed without a dilution model
anti_rework_rules.example: an option-pool refresh agreed without modeling founder stake

anti_rework_rules.rule: set the price point before committing to acquisition channels
anti_rework_rules.rationale: channel-price mismatch makes CAC unviable and forces rework
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: channels chosen before the price is known
anti_rework_rules.example: field sales staffed before realizing the price is low-touch

anti_rework_rules.rule: pass dependency, validation, and review gates before hard-locking artifacts
anti_rework_rules.rationale: premature hard locks commit irreversibly on unproven foundations
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a hard lock appears before its gates pass
anti_rework_rules.example: a scaling plan hard-locked while fit is unproven

anti_rework_rules.rule: produce a handoff artifact after each major workflow step
anti_rework_rules.rationale: missing handoffs lose context across sessions and reviewers
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a completed step with no handoff artifact
anti_rework_rules.example: fit assessment finished with no decision record passed downstream

iteration_protocol.trigger: a validation or experiment threshold is missed
acceptance_tests: failure is logged with a route

iteration_protocol.trigger: multiple defects are open at once
iteration_protocol.detection: rank by risk and downstream rework
action: score defects by risk and coupling

iteration_protocol.trigger: a fix touches a high-coupling or soft-locked node
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: impact set is stable across a pass

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is assigned for repair
iteration_protocol.detection: map failure type to a repair owner
acceptance_tests: fix applied by the correct owner

iteration_protocol.trigger: a repair changes a locked or high-coupling component
iteration_protocol.detection: rerun validator and affected acceptance tests
action: rerun acceptance tests in the impact set
acceptance_tests: validator passes and tests in scope pass

iteration_protocol.trigger: new evidence shifts a prior importance or confidence
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: posterior change is below the revisit delta

iteration_protocol.trigger: fit reverses or runway crosses the decision horizon
iteration_protocol.detection: monitor fit signals and runway monthly
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: a decision is recorded for the current cycle

iteration_protocol.trigger: all gates pass and defects are resolved
iteration_protocol.detection: confirm validator pass and gate completion
acceptance_tests: validator passes and gates are complete
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no open defects and gates passed

mandatory_checks.description: output is strict valid JSON with no markdown or comments
no template placeholders survive
edge_type and evidence labels use closed enum values only
all required top-level keys present
every major node references at least one competency question
source registry complete and includes SRC_HEURISTIC_PRIOR
node IDs unique
edge IDs unique and well-formed
edge, dependency, workflow, edge-case, conflict-axis, source, and CQ references resolve
dependencies and conflicts are not conflated
dependency graph is acyclic
scores and probabilities in 0..1 and signed_tension in -1..1
formula variables defined and present in score_derivation_inputs
score_derivation_input_labels complete for AT, DG, UR, RT
computed scores consistent with formulas within tolerance
evidence labels legal and no observed labels without observed data
probabilistic layer complete with valid uncertainty interval
high-risk nodes have acceptance tests and human review
high-coupling nodes have revisit triggers
workflow steps have entry, inputs, outputs, gates, tests, and exit criteria
conflict edges and axes have resolution rules and dominance logic
priority_order and priority_rationale cover every node exactly once
no hard lock before dependency, validation, and review gates pass
validation report records pass/fail/warning per mandatory class
traceability matrix links sources, CQs, nodes, edges, workflow, validation, artifacts
